label: Scheme Machine
line: A true scheme told in the third person: the result first, the scheme as a loop, the one number or one sentence that makes it work, the tell, and a second layer in the last line.
best_for: a scam, a fraud, a loophole or an exploit that works as a loop
a system that paid out twice: a billing loop, an arbitrage, a reward someone farmed
also_for: a weakness or an attack with one actor who meant it
avoid_for: a mechanism that needs more than four steps
an opinion dressed as a scheme
signals: someone gained from it on purpose
the trick repeats as a loop
the loop has four steps or fewer
it was caught, closed or named a crime

beats.name: The result
beats.job: Who got what from whom, as a number.

beats.name: The offer at full strength
beats.job: Why it looked legitimate, or the rule being used.

beats.name: The machine
beats.job: The loop in one sentence, three or four steps, the last feeding the first.

beats.name: The trick and the tell
beats.job: The one number or one mechanism sentence that makes it work, then one concrete detail anyone could have spotted.

beats.name: Scale
beats.job: The total, as a number against something the viewer knows.

beats.name: Second layer
beats.job: The motive, the multiplier or the outcome. The last line.

hooks.shape: [An ordinary person, by role] built [a machine for free money] and took [amount], [legally or unnoticed].
[A crew] took [amount] from [institution] without ever [doing the obvious crime].
[A fee of N percent] against [M percent back]. That gap paid [someone] [amount].

holds: The result is given and the method is held back. The method then arrives as a machine with one number at its heart, and the viewer asks 'would I have spotted it?'. The trick lands in the middle; what waits for the end is a second layer.
ending: The outcome, the motive or the multiplier. No list of ways to protect yourself.
template: [A person, by role] took [amount] from [institution or victims], [legally or unnoticed]. It looked legitimate because [the offer at full strength]. Behind it: [step 1], then [step 2], then [step 3], which fed [step 1]. It worked because [the cost] was smaller than [the gain]. The giveaway was [one concrete detail]. By the end, [the scale against a benchmark]. And [the second layer].
